newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India expected to buy 500,000-700,000/T Feb diesel.
newsitem.headline: India expected to buy 500,000-700,000/T Feb diesel.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is expected to buy between 500,000 and over 700,000 tonnes of high speed diesel in its tender for February delivery, traders said on Friday.
But some traders said judging from the relatively small volumes that India had bought over the past four months, they were not optimistic that IOC would take more than 500,000 tonnes this time.
"India would have to buy more, we have said that for the past three to four months," one trader said. "But consistently they have awarded less than expected."
Another trader said it was now more difficult to estimate what India would actually take, because unlike in the past, "what they planned now is not what they would buy."
Traders said one reason for this is India's tight foreign exchange situation and recent high spot prices were making it difficult for them to buy more.
India's recent diesel imports included 120,000 tonnes in October, none in November, 520,000 tonnes in December and 345,000 tonnes in January.
Traders said in IOC's latest tender for 1.0-percent sulphur diesel, which closed on December 18, most offers were based on the high of Mediterranean spot quotes rather than MidEast spot quotes.
"The Mediterranean is a good source of supply for the moment than the MidEast," one trader said.
Traders said offers were aggressive with west coast cargoes seen around $24.00-$25.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, cost and freight (c-and-f) basis.
Low offers to the east coast were seen around $26.00 and $28.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f.

In its second tender for January delivery, IOC purcased two 45,000-tonne cargoes of 0.5 percent sulphur diesel at $25.85 and $25.88 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f Kandla, from Stinnes and Shell.
